versions.title_at_revision: Verify that the stores/air vehicle interface does not create unsafe conditions during ground and flight operations and that no unsafe environment is created for maintenance personnel.
versions.text: Verify that the stores/air vehicle interface does not create unsafe conditions during ground and flight operations and that no unsafe environment is created for maintenance personnel.

Criterion: Verify that the stores/air vehicle interface does not create unsafe conditions during ground and flight operations and that no unsafe environment is created for maintenance personnel. Standard: Clearance between store and surroundings (such as Alternative Mission Equipment (AME), racks, and launchers) is sufficient to allow for stores loading, aircraft/munitions servicing, in flight vibration and deployment without contacting air vehicle, AME and other stores. Stores loading/unloading procedures are defined and documented. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analysis, test, demonstration, simulation, inspection and review of documentation. Stores/air vehicle interface is verified by test in accordance with STANAG 3899, MIL-HDBK-1763, MIL-STD-1289 and MIL-STD-8591. Safe separation certification, Non-Nuclear Munitions Safety Board Certification, and Weapon System Explosive Safety Review Board (WSESRB) concurrence are achieved. Loading of aircraft is verified by Validation/Verification (Val/Ver) testing. Stores loading/unloading procedures are verified by demonstration using the stores loading manual. References: MIL-STD-1289 MIL-HDBK-1763 MIL-STD-8591 STANAG 3899 ADS-44-HDBK ADS-45-HDBK

Standard: Stores meet minimum clearance requirements IAW MIL-STD-1289, Clearances section during all phases of ground and flight operations. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Analysis shows the store OML is the same, or has minimal differences, from a previously certified store.
(2) Virtual or analytical fit check shows clearance requirements are met IAW MIL-STD-1289, Clearances section.
(3) Dynamic deflection analysis ensures stores do not contact the air vehicle, pylon, ground or other stores during all phases of flight.
(4) For rotary-wing air vehicles, analysis verifies that projectiles do not contact rotor blades during dynamic maneuvers IAW MIL-STD-1289, Clearances section. Test.
  (1) Ground test: Verify that physical fit and clearance requirements are met IAW MIL-STD- 1289, Clearances section and MIL-HDBK-1763, Test 101 for all store configurations.
  (2) Ground test: Verify that fired munitions and projectiles have clearance from the air vehicle or other stores IAW MIL-STD-1289, Clearances section and Installation Test Methods section and MIL HDBK-1763, Test 160. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (3) Flight test: Verify stores do not contact the air vehicle or adjacent stores throughout the operational envelope.
  (4) Flight test: Verify that fired munitions and projectiles do not contact the air vehicle or other stores IAW MIL HDBK-1763, Test 273 and Test 274.
